info.bio: Consolidated are an American radical recording and performing collective, formed in in San Francisco in 1988. They were distinguished by left-leaning political activism and politically radical lyrics, as well as their innovative sonic collages which blended industrial and hip-hop styles. Adam Sherburne and Mark Pistel had been members of synthpop/dance outfit Until December.  Philip Steir had drummed in the funk/rock group Shy Hands. Repudiating those bands' sound and politics

scenes.name: Rap y hip hop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: A finales de los ochenta el «rockero» es una figura tan obsoleta como lo fue el cantante pop en 1956: tres revoluciones toman la música popular (el DJ como fuerza creativa, el hip hop y la fusión ciberpunk de industrial, metal y hardcore). En 1975 Kool Herc reinventa el breakbeat en el Bronx; el rap es una evolución del dub jamaicano. Sugar Hill Gang, Kurtis Blow, los «mensajes» de Grandmaster Flash, Afrika Bambaataa (el Leonardo del beatbox, inventor del «electro»), el tocadiscos como instrumento, Run-DMC, Tackhead, L.L. Cool J, Eric B & Rakim y Public Enemy (It Takes A Nation Of Millions, la obra maestra del hip hop). El gangsta rap (Schoolly D, NWA, Ice Cube, Dr Dre, 2Pac), Beastie Boys, las raperas (MC Lyte, Queen Latifah), De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest, Cypress Hill; en Gran Bretaña, Art Of Noise.

podcast.title: Manifesting Mixed Styles
podcast.body: Consolidated was noted as one of the "new groups" whose work at the end of the 1980s demonstrated the emerging coexistence and blending of rock, rap, and hip hop styles, contributing to the broader palette of Alt Rock. "It was manifested in the work of new groups, with names like Consolidated at MC900Foot Jesus."

xref.title: Beatles' Release Strategy (1963-1965)
xref.body: During 1963-1965, The Beatles employed a prolific release strategy, putting out up to a dozen singles per year, which were then consolidated into two annual albums, a model cited as a precedent for the constant flow of new music required from artists today. "Artists need to deliver a constant flow of new songs, just like the Beatles did through the year 1963, 64 and 65, when they'd release up to a dozen singles and then summarize them with two albums a year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Founding and Location (1977)
xref.body: The Power Station, located in New York at approximately 53rd and 10th, was founded in 1977 by Tony Bongiovi, the second cousin of John Bon Jovi. The building previously served as a Consolidated Edison power plant and later a TV studio for "Let's Make a Deal." "In 1977, the building was bought and rebuilt as a recording studio by Tony Bongeovi, the second cousin of some New Jersey kid named John Bongeovi."
